newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: MeesPierson good buy for Fortis - analysts.
newsitem.headline: MeesPierson good buy for Fortis - analysts.

text.p: Dutch investment bank MeesPierson would be a good buy for Fortis as the Dutch-Belgian financial group was underdeveloped in the field of investment and private banking, insurance analysts said on Thursday .
"It is a good fit," said Nico van Geest of Suez Securities, adding an acquisition price of around 2.5 billion would be very reasonable.
Earlier today Fortis confirmed it was in talks with ABN AMRO over the purchase of its unit, MeesPierson.

"ABN AMRO might be willing to make concessions to the buyer if it were Fortis, and accept a bid of around 2.2 billion guilders as MeesPierson would remain in Dutch hands," he said, adding ABN AMRO would not be willing to invite foreign compatitors into its own backyard.

On Tuesday ABN AMRO said it was in talks about the possible sale of MeesPierson. There has long been speculation that ABN AMRO would divest MeesPierson, especially after ABN AMRO bought in 1992 the London-based securities house Hoare Govett, a competitor of MeesPierson.

Heinie Hakker of Barclays de Zoete Wedd said he expected Fortis was the only discussion partner left for ABN AMRO on the acquisition of MeesPierson. "I think they are the partner involved in the talks," he said, adding talks were probably near to conclusion.
"The acquisition of MeesPierson would add to the earnings per share of Fortis," he said.
Analyst Jacob Boscha of Labouchere said he was a believer in the Bancassurance concept and that Fortis' business would be more in balance if Fortis managed to acquire MeesPierson.

"In Belgium Fortis is already a strong player in the banking sector since it acquired a part of ASLK," he said. "The acquisition of MeesPierson would be a big step forward for the Dutch side of Fortis," he said.
Analysts were divided on the way Fortis would pay for MeesPierson if the acquisition went ahead.
"Fortis Amev (which with Belgium's Fortis AG jointly own Fortis) could decide on the issue of new shares," said Van Geest of Suez Securities.

He said the firm could decide to issue another five percent, or at the most 10 percent, of shares, adding the sum might also be paid with its own recources. "A new issue is possible, not necessary," he said.
Heinie Hakker said not all business groups of MeesPierson would fit in if Fortis acquired MeesPierson with all its units.
"MeesPierson does not fit for a 100 percent," he said, adding he was curious to hear if brokers Wesselius and Gilissen, both units of MeesPierson, were included in the talks.
